lead.headline: Inference economics turn on memory movement, not just faster chips
lead.dek: A synthetic serving study illustrates the evidence needed to connect a systems improvement to a lower cost per request.
paragraphs: In this layout fixture, a hypothetical engineering team separates model loading, prefill and decoding before comparing serving paths. Faster transfer alone would not establish a production gain: queueing, cache reuse and the latency target determine how much capacity becomes usable.

The mechanism belongs in the story. Moving fewer bytes between memory tiers could free bandwidth, but the result depends on model size, concurrency and context length. The illustrative comparison below is test data dated October 2, 2026, not a vendor result or a forecast.

stories.dek: Pre-warmed engines narrow the gap between process failure and restored token service.

blocks.text: A new recovery design keeps initialized capacity ready to take over without repeating the full model startup path. The operational value is predictable failover rather than another peak-throughput claim.

blocks.text: This synthetic research brief preserves the mechanism: a hypothetical experiment changes the collection angle of an optical system, then compares resolution and depth of focus.
